primary_question: Does state-transition-driven replanning with deduplication improve dynamic-failure rescue service over B/Bprime without unsafe action or excessive computation?

development.selection_rule: maximize mean rescue service, sustained 30-second recovery, and first full recovery in lexicographic order; then minimize censoring time, decision wall time, decision count; ties prefer 20 seconds

event_policy.input_visibility: current network state, current snapshot, current diagnosis and battery only
event_triggers: return-reserve margin crossing the 25 Wh alert boundary
event_policy.timeout_semantics: post-search output watchdog; late result is discarded and a no-deploy safety decision is issued; synchronous Python search is not preempted

runtime_safety: all policies use the same simulation actuator and radio constraints
maximum movement per tick is speed_km_per_s times time_step_s
route must remain inside city boundaries and return to a healthy station within reserve
backhaul/access range and shared capacity checks stay enabled
actual runtime energy is charged once per tick

recovery_metrics.first_full_recovery: first simulation tick with every rescue user connected
recovery_metrics.sustained_recovery: all rescue users connected for at least 30 continuous simulation seconds
recovery_metrics.unrecovered: failure retained; horizon used only in recovery-or-censoring paired analysis
recovery_metrics.decision_compute: wall-clock perf_counter around observe, separately reported from simulation time

statistics.paired_continuous: per-seed mean, median, sample SD, 95% Student-t CI, Cohen dz, Hedges gz and two-sided exact sign-flip randomization
statistics.paired_binary: Wilson CI and paired exact McNemar binomial test
statistics.multiple_comparisons: Holm correction separately for efficacy and resource/cost metrics across scenes and E versus B/Bprime
statistics.latency: conditional successful user-time samples per strategy, with sample counts; no paired inference
